main_body: Timber-framed house with a large red tile hip roof, a front gable dormer, a chimney, plaster-and-timber walls, a door and a window, plus a lower porch/entrance block with a door
top_band: Roof tile slopes, light orange tiles with dark red courses, from about row 2 to row 43 (ridge cap highlighted at rows 0-5), clearly lighter than the walls and separated from them by the dark eave beam
evidence: The roof is drawn as large sloped surfaces: hip planes on both sides, a front gable, and a ridge with highlights. It sits above the vertical plaster and timber walls. A dark eave band (rows ~42-45) shadows the wall top. The window, doors and timber frames are inset with dark edges. The lower porch block has the same structure as the main house. It matches the Beodeul house references, where a roof over a wall counts as the visible top. No isometric side face.

style.evidence: Median colours per tile is 18, equal to house-h101_0 and above house-h112_0-stone (11). Flat-fill coverage is 0% and there are 202 distinct colours, more than either reference. Only 12% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted dark brown or red-brown beside the materials. The roof has per-tile highlights and several tones. The plaster is speckled and the timber has grain. It sits at the reference level next to both references, so it does not look thinner or more sticker-like.
